pesto.title: Kitchen to Table — Basil Pesto in 5 Weeks
pesto.excerpt: A simple recipe series showing how to go from pod to plate with your first PlantyHub harvest.
body: Your first basil pods usually reach harvest around weeks three to five — snip the tips and the plant keeps growing.
For a quick pesto, blend a handful of fresh basil with olive oil, garlic, pine nuts and hard cheese until smooth. Season with salt and lemon.
The difference from shop herbs is immediate: brighter aroma and pesto that tastes like a garden, not a fridge.
Store pesto in a jar with a thin layer of oil on top — it keeps for several days in the fridge. Or freeze in ice-cube trays for winter.
After harvesting, leave the garden on its cycle. A new basil or mint pod in the next slot keeps something fresh on the counter.

hydroponics.title: Why Hydroponics Uses 90% Less Water
hydroponics.excerpt: The science behind smart indoor gardens and why they're the sustainable choice for urban homes.
body: In soil gardens, water is lost to runoff and evaporation. A closed hydroponic tray recirculates only what roots need.
With HomeGarder One, metered light and steady moisture let plants invest in leaves instead of surviving drought.
For city households that means fewer top-ups, less waste and herbs that keep producing for months.
Hydroponics is not a lab experiment — it is a quiet counter that works while you cook. Less water, less stress, more flavour.

spices.title: Aromatic Spices You Can Grow on the Counter
spices.excerpt: Thyme, oregano, rosemary, chives and chili — the spice drawer, reinvented as living pods.
body: Culinary spices do not have to arrive only dried. Slow aromatics like thyme, oregano and rosemary thrive under steady LED light.
Chives give a soft onion note for eggs and soups. Chillies bring heat once fruits start to colour.
Fill a few slots with our spice pods — or take the 12-pod mix — and season straight from the crown while you cook.
Harvest little and often: live spices smell best when the leaf was just cut, not sitting for days in a plastic box.

first-harvest.title: How to Take Your First Harvest Without Stress
first-harvest.excerpt: A calm checklist for week two and three: what to snip, what to leave, and how often to feed.
body: Wait until the plant has several true leaves before the first cut. Never take more than one third of the canopy at once.
Harvest in the morning when essential oils are strongest. Use clean scissors and cut above a leaf node so it branches.
Keep the nutrient solution and light cycle steady — a stressed plant turns bitter before it looks bad.
If you are unsure, start with basil or mint: they forgive easy mistakes and quickly show whether your garden rhythm is right.

partnership.title: PlantyHub × Sustainable Living EU
partnership.excerpt: We teamed up with eco-conscious creators to show how one garden can change your daily routine.
body: Together with Sustainable Living EU we followed homes that replaced shop-bought herbs with a countertop garden.
Creators logged setup time, top-ups and taste — most cooked with their own harvest within a month.
The takeaway is simple: when growing is automatic, fresh herbs stop being a special occasion.
Small habits add up — less plastic from clamshell packs, fewer wilted herbs, more dinners scented with what you grew yourself.

earthday.title: Earth Day: Grow Your Own, Waste Less
earthday.excerpt: How biodegradable pods and home growing help cut plastic and food waste.
body: Shop herbs often wilt unused. When you cut only what you need, flavour arrives without a half-empty box.
Pods are designed to compost after their cycle, and the garden lasts for years with refills.
A small kitchen garden will not fix the climate alone — but it changes habits, and habits multiply.
Start with one pod. Then two. After a month your kitchen speaks a different language — harvest, not waste.

faqPage.title: Frequently asked questions
faqPage.lead: Everything about HomeGarder One, pods, shipping, warranty and plant care — in one place.
faqPage.ctaText: Write to us — we reply within one business day.

items.q: Where do you ship?
items.a: For now we ship only in Bulgaria. Orders usually leave within 24 hours on business days.

items.q: How much is shipping?
items.a: Shipping is calculated at checkout for an address in Bulgaria. Over €150, shipping is free.

items.q: How long does delivery take?
items.a: Typically 1–3 business days, depending on the courier and the town.

items.q: How do I track my order?
items.a: Once shipped, you get an email with a tracking number and courier link. You can also check status under My orders if you have an account.

items.q: Can I change the address after ordering?
items.a: Yes, if the parcel has not shipped yet. Email support@plantyhub.com immediately with your order number and new address.

items.q: What if my parcel arrives damaged?
items.a: Photograph the packaging and product and contact us within 48 hours. We will replace it or arrange a return at no extra cost to you.

items.q: Do you ship outside Bulgaria?
items.a: Not at the moment. We deliver only in Bulgaria.

items.q: Do I get an invoice?
items.a: Yes. Consumers receive a receipt/invoice as required. Companies can add billing details at checkout or email us after ordering.

items.q: What is HomeGarder One?
items.a: A smart hydroponic countertop garden: full-spectrum LED light, automatic watering and room for multiple pods — no soil and no gardening experience needed.

items.q: What is in the box?
items.a: The garden unit, LED arm, power supply, starter pods (depending on bundle), nutrient solution A and B and a quick-start guide with QR instructions.

items.q: How long does first setup take?
items.a: Usually 10–15 minutes: unpack, attach the light, fill with water, insert pods and plug in.

items.q: Do I need Wi‑Fi or an app?
items.a: Not required for core use. The garden runs on its own light cycle. If connectivity features are available, the manual covers them.

items.q: How many pod slots are there?
items.a: HomeGarder One grows several pods at once — typically up to 12 depending on the model and kit. See the product page for exact specs.

items.q: Is it noisy?
items.a: No — designed for kitchens and living rooms. Pump and light stay quiet in normal use.

items.q: Where should I place it?
items.a: On a stable counter near a socket, away from ovens and strong drafts. Leave airflow around the lamp and do not block vents.

items.q: What are the size and weight?
items.a: It is a compact desktop garden — exact dimensions and weight are listed in the HomeGarder One specifications.

items.q: How much power does it use?
items.a: The LED system is efficient — roughly like a few LED bulbs. Usage depends on brightness and the 16/8 light cycle.

items.q: Do I need gardening experience?
items.a: No. Insert a pod, add water and nutrients, and the light follows an automatic cycle. QR instructions guide every step.

items.q: When is the first harvest?
items.a: Most herbs are ready for a first trim about 2–4 weeks after sprouting and keep producing for weeks or months with good care.

items.q: How should I harvest?
items.a: Snip tips and outer leaves rather than the whole plant so it branches and keeps producing. Use clean scissors.

items.q: What light cycle should I use?
items.a: About 16 hours light and 8 hours dark. Avoid interrupting the cycle often — plants need rest.

items.q: What temperature works best?
items.a: Ideally 18–26°C. Avoid long periods below 15°C or above 30°C — that slows sprouting and growth.

items.q: Why are my plants pale or weak?
items.a: Check water level, that the lamp runs a full cycle, that pods are not expired, and that nutrients are dosed as instructed.

items.q: Can I grow year-round?
items.a: Yes — that is the point of indoor hydroponics. You only need water, light and nutrients.

items.q: My plants smell odd — is that normal?
items.a: Fresh herbs should smell pleasant. A stagnant-water smell means drain, rinse the tank and refill with clean nutrient solution.

items.q: What can I grow?
items.a: Basil, mint, parsley, cilantro, dill, arugula, green onion and more from our catalog. Every HomeGarder pod fits the slots.

items.q: What is inside a pod?
items.a: Pre-seeded seeds in a hydroponic medium, ready to insert. Non-GMO seeds as per our product policy.

items.q: How long do unused pods last?
items.a: Store dry and cool in the original packaging. Check the date on the pack — do not use heavily expired pods.

items.q: What are solutions A and B?
items.a: A two-part nutrient system for hydroponics. Mix with water as directed — never mix concentrates together undiluted.

items.q: How often should I top up water?
items.a: Check a few times a week. Plants drink more in warm weather and as they grow larger. Never let the tank run dry.

items.q: When should I replace the nutrient solution?
items.a: Usually every 2–4 weeks, or sooner if growth slows or leaves change colour. Drain, rinse lightly and refill fresh.

items.q: My pod will not sprout — what now?
items.a: Wait 7–14 days. Check water, light and temperature. If nothing happens, email us with your order number — we replace pods under our sprouting policy.

items.q: Can I reuse a pod?
items.a: Not recommended. After harvest, insert a fresh pod for a clean restart.

items.q: Where do I buy more pods?
items.a: In the Pods section of the site. Mix flavours and add nutrients or accessories in the same order.

items.q: How do I clean the garden?
items.a: Unplug, drain the water, wash the tank with a soft sponge and clean water. Avoid harsh cleaners on electronics and the LED panel.

items.q: How often should I clean?
items.a: Light cleaning when you refresh nutrients; deeper clean every 1–2 months or when replacing all pods.

items.q: What about algae in the tank?
items.a: Reduce light reaching the water (pod caps help), wash the tank and change the water. Algae love light and stagnant water.

items.q: The light will not turn on — how do I check?
items.a: Check the socket, adapter and cable connection. If it still fails, contact us — it may be covered by warranty.

items.q: The pump is not circulating?
items.a: Make sure there is enough water and the intake is not blocked. Restart the unit. If it still fails, contact support.

items.q: Is it safe around kids and pets?
items.a: Keep cables tidy and do not let anyone drink from the tank. Nutrient solution is not for consumption. Avoid staring into the LED up close for long.

items.q: Can I move it while running?
items.a: Better to unplug and partially drain first to avoid spills. Move carefully — a full tank is heavy.

items.q: What warranty do I get?
items.a: HomeGarder One includes a 2-year warranty for manufacturing defects. Keep your order number and proof of purchase.

items.q: What is the return policy?
items.a: You have 30 days to return if you are not satisfied, subject to return conditions (condition and completeness). Contact us for a label/instructions.

items.q: How do I start a warranty claim?
items.a: Email support@plantyhub.com with a description, photos/video and order number. We will guide diagnosis or replacement.

items.q: What is not covered?
items.a: Damage from misuse, drops, water on electronics outside normal operation, unauthorised repairs, or used consumables (pods, nutrients).

items.q: How long do refunds take?
items.a: After we receive and inspect the return, refunds usually take a few business days depending on your bank/card.

items.q: Can I replace only the lamp or pump?
items.a: Often yes, depending on diagnosis. Do not discard the part before contacting us.

items.q: Which payment methods do you accept?
items.a: Card and other methods shown at checkout. Online payments use a secure process.

items.q: Are prices VAT inclusive?
items.a: Store prices are in euros. Taxes/VAT depend on shipping address and appear clearly before you pay.

items.q: Do I need an account?
items.a: Not required to buy, but an account makes tracking orders and reordering pods easier.

items.q: How do I reset my password?
items.a: On the login page choose Forgot password? and follow the email link. Check spam if it does not arrive, or contact us.

items.q: How does the newsletter discount work?
items.a: After subscribing you get a code (e.g. 5% off first order). Enter it at checkout before paying. One code per order unless stated otherwise.

items.q: Do you offer business / bulk pricing?
items.a: Yes. Email support@plantyhub.com with approximate quantities and location.

items.q: How do I unsubscribe from emails?
items.a: Every marketing email has an unsubscribe link. Transactional order emails may still be sent when needed.

items.q: Is my data protected?
items.a: We process personal data under our privacy policy for orders, support and (with consent) marketing.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.lead: This policy describes the cookies and similar technologies plantyhub.com uses so the store can work and — only with your consent — measure visits and ads.

sections.title: What they are
paragraphs: Cookies are small text files a site or an outside service stores in your browser. Entries in localStorage and sessionStorage play a similar role: they stay on your device and are not sent to our server on their own each time you open a page.

sections.title: Your choice
paragraphs: On a first visit, if analytics or advertising tools are switched on, we show a banner. Accept turns on all non-essential tools at once. Reject leaves them off. Essential storage for the cart, language and sign-in does not depend on the banner.

The choice is stored locally in the browser under the key plantyhub.cookie-consent. You can change it at any time from Cookie settings in the footer. If you reject, we stop further collection and clear Google, Meta and Clarity cookies already set, as far as the browser allows.

sections.title: Essential
paragraphs: These entries are needed to shop, stay signed in and remember the language. The basis is that the service cannot work without them. Without them the cart, sign-in or checkout may fail.
items: Cart (plantyhub_cart) — the products you added, until you remove them or clear the browser
Language (plantyhub-lang-choice) — the language you picked
Sign-in — an account token and basic account details in localStorage if you choose to be remembered, or in sessionStorage until you close the browser
Newsletter banner (ph_newsletter_seen) — so the popup does not return after you have seen it
Cookie choice (plantyhub.cookie-consent) — remembers whether you accepted or rejected
During payment, Stripe or PayPal may set their own cookies needed to take the payment and reduce fraud

sections.title: Analytics
paragraphs: These load only if you accept. We use them to see which pages are opened and where the site is hard to use. We do not use them for a decision that produces legal effects for you.
The site loads only the tools listed here. A new tool will not start until we add it to this policy.
items: Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager (Google Ireland Limited) — cookies such as _ga, _ga_* and _gid; they measure visits and pages
Microsoft Clarity (Microsoft) — cookies such as _clck and _clsk; they show, in aggregate, how pages are used, for example scrolling and clicks
If an ad click sets a _gcl_* cookie, it belongs to Google and usually lasts up to 90 days. If you reject, we clear it with the others.

sections.title: QR codes on the packaging
paragraphs: The box, the pods and the printed guide carry a QR code to plantyhub.com/start. The address may include a from parameter with the value box, pods or instr. It only shows which label was scanned and does not identify you. The parameter itself is not a cookie.

If you accept cookies, the page address — including that parameter — is recorded by the tools in this policy, because they measure the page you open. We also send Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager a qr_open event with the label, so we can see where people scan from. If you reject, we send neither the address to those tools nor the event.

sections.title: Marketing
paragraphs: These load with the same consent as analytics. They show which ads lead to visits and purchases, and can be used to show our ads again to people who have visited the site (remarketing).

startPage.title: Your garden in 6 steps
startPage.lead: Ready to plant in about 5 minutes.
startPage.videoCaption: A short upright video of the setup.
startPage.videoMissing: The video is not uploaded yet. It will play here once the file is ready.
startPage.moreLead: Doses, care and timing. Open only what you need.
startPage.stepsLead: From an empty garden to the first leaves. Each step takes about a minute.

steps.title: Fill with water
steps.text: Pour 4 L of water into the tank. Filtered or low-mineral bottled water is better; tap water is fine. Aim for about 18–24 °C. Set the garden on a stable counter, near a socket.

steps.title: Add A and B
steps.text: On the first fill, add 5 ml of A, stir, then 5 ml of B — up to the green line on the cap. Always A first, then B, and do not mix them undiluted. On a water change, use 8 ml of A and 8 ml of B, up to the red line.

steps.title: Place the pods
steps.text: Peel off the sticker, put one pod in each slot, and set a cap on top. Do not open a pod before you place it. Keep unused pods cool and dry, in the original pack.

steps.title: Set the lamp
steps.text: Lower the lamp close over the caps. Once leaves appear, keep it at least 2 cm above them. It runs on its own: 16 hours of light and 8 hours of rest. The cycle starts when you switch it on — do not turn it off at night.

steps.title: Remove the caps
steps.text: Take the cap off as soon as the sprout reaches it. Until then the cap holds moisture and shades the water. If a sprout reaches the cap sooner, take it off straight away.

steps.title: Harvest and trim
steps.text: Between water changes, top up with clean water only and harvest regularly. Cut above a pair of leaves and take no more than about a third at once. The plant branches and grows back.

startPage.doseLead: Both fills are for 4 L of water. The line is on the bottle cap.
startPage.doseNote: Between changes, top up with clean water only. One pack lasts about 12 fills. The lamp runs automatically. The cycle starts when you switch it on.
startPage.careLead: Change the water and clean every 2–3 weeks. Unplug before you do.

careItems.title: Topping up
careItems.text: Between changes, add clean water only.

careItems.title: Change and clean
careItems.text: Every 2–3 weeks, rinse and refill with 8 ml A + 8 ml B in 4 L.

careItems.title: Lamp
careItems.text: At least 2 cm above the leaves. Do not break the 16/8 cycle.

careItems.title: Safety
careItems.text: Keep away from children. The water is not for drinking. Indoor only. Fit a new pod after harvest.

startPage.plantsTitle: When they sprout and when to harvest
startPage.plantsLead: These times are a guide. They depend on water, temperature and light.
startPage.waterLead: Water is the base of hydroponics.
waterBest: Filtered water — from a filter jug or a reverse-osmosis system. Soft, without chlorine, and the most predictable result.
Bottled spring or table water with low mineral content. On the label: total mineralisation under about 300 mg/L.
Distilled water. It works well — solution A and B add the calcium and magnesium the plants need.
startPage.waterOk: Leave it uncovered for a few hours so the chlorine leaves. Hard water can leave limescale on the tank walls — switch to filtered water if that happens.
waterNo: Mineral or alkaline water — high pH and a lot of salts
Water from a salt softener — the sodium harms the roots
waterPrep: Use water at room temperature, about 18–24 °C.
Pour 4 L into the tank and add the solution: 5 ml of A up to the green line on the cap, stir, then 5 ml of B.
Between changes, top up with the same kind of water, without solution.
startPage.waterCareLead: Six things that keep the garden healthy.

waterCare.title: Water level
waterCare.text: Do not let it drop below the minimum mark. The pump then runs dry, gets noisy and can be damaged. Check every 2–3 days, especially when the plants are large.

waterCare.title: Cloudy water or a smell
waterCare.text: Change the water straight away. Do not wait the usual 2–3 weeks.

waterCare.title: Algae
waterCare.text: Green in the tank. Cover the empty slots and do not leave the garden in direct sun.

waterCare.title: Cleaning
waterCare.text: Water and a soft sponge only, no detergents. For limescale you can use diluted vinegar, then rinse well.

waterCare.title: Old water
waterCare.text: You can pour it on potted plants or in the garden. It is diluted fertiliser.

waterCare.title: Warm water
waterCare.text: Above about 26 °C the roots do not get enough oxygen and they rot. This matters in summer.

startPage.afterLead: Everything you need once the garden is planted.
startPage.stageNote: The first harvest is within 6 weeks of planting. Plants grow faster in a warmer room and with filtered water. After the first cut they keep growing, and if you harvest properly they give fresh leaves for weeks.

stages.title: Sprouting
stages.text: The first small sprouts under the cap.

stages.title: First harvest
stages.text: Enough leaves for the first handful.

stages.title: Full size
stages.text: The plants are dense and you can harvest every day.

startPage.harvestRule: Do not take more than a third at once. Cut with clean scissors — do not pull by hand, or you may lift the whole pod out.

harvestRows.name: Basil
harvestRows.how: Pinch the tip just above a pair of leaves.
harvestRows.why: Two new shoots appear and the plant grows denser.

harvestRows.name: Parsley
harvestRows.how: Cut the outer stems at the base.
harvestRows.why: New stems grow from the centre.

harvestRows.name: Lettuce
harvestRows.how: Take the outer leaves and leave the centre.
harvestRows.why: The centre keeps making new leaves.

startPage.harvestNote: When the plants reach the lamp raised all the way, trim the tips the same way. If basil flowers, pinch the flowers off — otherwise the leaves turn bitter.
startPage.faqLead: Most problems take a minute to fix. Find what you see.

faqs.a: The room is too cold, the cap came off too early, or the pod is not reaching the water. Check the cap, the temperature (18–24 °C) and the water level. If it still does not sprout, email us.
The lamp is too far away and the plants are reaching for the light. Lower it to 2 cm above the leaves.
The solution is used up or the water is old. Change the water and add 8 ml A + 8 ml B, up to the red line on the cap.
The water is too warm, above about 26 °C, and the roots are short of oxygen. Change it for cooler water and move the garden away from a radiator or the sun.
Bacteria have grown in the water. Change it straight away and rinse the tank.
That is algae — light is reaching the water. Cover the empty slots and do not leave the garden in direct sun.
The level has dropped below the minimum mark. Top up with clean water. Run dry, the pump gets noisy and can be damaged.

startPage.orderHint: When the harvest is done, take out the old pods, rinse the tank and start again. 12 new pods including VAT are €14.99 and fill the whole garden. One pack of solution A and B lasts about 12 fills.
startPage.warranty: If a pod does not sprout and you followed the instructions, we send a new one free.
claimSteps: Wait 3 weeks from planting. Some seeds are simply slower.
Photograph the garden so the pod without sprouts is visible.
Send the photo to sales@plantyhub.com with your order number and the batch from the box.
We will send a new pod of the same kind.
startPage.academyText: If you want more lessons, photos and video, open the academy.
startPage.safetyText: Solution B — DANGER: causes serious eye damage. Solution A — WARNING: causes serious eye irritation. Keep the solutions and pods away from children — the pods are small parts. Not for drinking. Wear eye protection. If in eyes: rinse carefully with water for several minutes, remove contact lenses if you can, and keep rinsing. Get medical help. Toxicology centre: 02 9154 233. Store the solutions tightly closed, at 10–30 °C, away from heat, freezing and direct sunlight. Unplug the garden before you change the water or clean it. Do not overfill the tank, and keep the adapter and cable dry. Keep the garden on a stable, level surface.

howPage.title: The garden waters and lights itself
howPage.lead: HomeGarder One has no soil. The roots drink from the tank, the lamp keeps its own cycle, and you add pods and harvest.
howPage.imageAlt: PlantyHub HomeGarder One on a kitchen counter
howPage.videoText: Water, pods and the lamp starting on its own. The same steps are written out below.
howPage.systemLead: You do not water every day, and you do not move the lamp on a clock.

systems.title: Water from below
systems.text: The tank holds 4 litres. A pump lifts water to the roots — no watering can and no soil.

systems.title: Food in two steps
systems.text: On the first fill you add 5 ml of A, stir, then 5 ml of B. Between changes you only top up with plain water.

systems.title: Light on a clock
systems.text: The cycle starts when you plug it in: 16 hours of light and 8 hours of rest. Do not switch it off at night.

howPage.stepsLead: Then the garden carries on by itself until it is time to harvest.

steps.title: Fill with water
steps.text: Pour in 4 L. Filtered or bottled is better; tap water works too. About 18–24 °C, on a stable counter near a socket.

steps.title: Add A and B
steps.text: First 5 ml of A to the green line, stir, then 5 ml of B. Do not mix them undiluted. When you change the water, the dose is 8 ml of each.

steps.title: Place the pods
steps.text: Peel the sticker, set one pod in each slot and a dome on top. The dome holds moisture until it sprouts.

steps.title: Set the lamp
steps.text: Lower it close to the domes. Once there are leaves, keep it at least 2 cm above them. The cycle is already running.

steps.title: Remove the domes
steps.text: Take the dome off as soon as the sprout touches it. Until then it shades the water and keeps the moisture in.

steps.title: Harvest and trim
steps.text: Cut above a pair of leaves and never take more than about a third at once. The plant branches and grows again.

howPage.waterTitle: Which water keeps the garden healthy
howPage.waterLead: Solutions A and B add the food. The water should be soft and about 18–24 °C.

waterGroups.title: Best
waterGroups.text: Filtered or reverse osmosis. Bottled water with mineralisation under about 300 mg/l. Distilled works too — A and B add the calcium and magnesium.

waterGroups.title: Fine
waterGroups.text: Leave it uncovered for a few hours so the chlorine leaves. If limescale appears on the tank walls, switch to filtered.

waterGroups.title: Don't use
waterGroups.text: Mineral or alkaline, sparkling, salt-softened water, hot water from the boiler, and rainwater.

howPage.growTitle: The first harvest is within six weeks
howPage.growLead: The times are a guide. In a warmer room and with filtered water the plants grow faster.

stages.title: Sprouting
stages.text: The first sprouts show under the dome.

stages.title: First harvest
stages.text: Enough leaves for the first handful.

stages.title: Every day
stages.text: The plants are full and keep giving fresh leaves for weeks.

howPage.harvestNote: Don't take more than a third at once, and cut with scissors so you don't pull the pod out. Pinch basil just above a pair of leaves — if it flowers, remove the flowers or the leaves turn bitter. Cut parsley from the outer stems. Cut arugula 2–3 cm above the base.
howPage.rhythmTitle: Between harvests there is one water change

rhythm.title: Top up
rhythm.text: Between changes, plain water only, no solution. Check every 2–3 days, especially when the plants are large.

rhythm.title: Change
rhythm.text: Every 2–3 weeks rinse the tank and add 8 ml of A and 8 ml of B to 4 L — to the red line. One pack lasts about 12 fills.

rhythm.title: The pump
rhythm.text: Don't let the level fall below the minimum mark. Running dry, the pump gets noisy and can be damaged.

rhythm.title: Empty slots
rhythm.text: Cover them. Light on the water grows algae. Don't keep the garden in direct sun.
